newsitem.title: UK: BT dismisses watchdog's inefficiency claims.
newsitem.headline: BT dismisses watchdog's inefficiency claims.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Tuesday dismissed allegations by industry watchdog Oftel that the company's network operations clocked up 40 million pounds ($65.4 million) worth of inefficiencies each year.
"We don't accept the basis on which this has been calculated," a company spokesman told Reuters.

The greater the inefficiencies identified by Oftel in the so-called "interconnect" charges -- which BT charges rivals for carrying calls on its network -- the tougher new regulatory price curbs are likely to be.
Oftel has already published a consultation document suggesting that a basket of interconnect prices should fall by 6-12 percent below the rate of retail price inflation from October.

But BT has charged that such price curbs would be "unduly harsh" on top of a 10-20 percent one-off price cut -- and said it might appeal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission if such caps were imposed.

The belated release of the inefficiencies identified by Oftel -- 3.5 percent of the total costs of BT's network operation -- was due to administration problems and does not affect the 6-12 percent price cut range already proposed, an Oftel spokeswoman said.
The consultation period ends on June 10 and BT said it would be meeting with the regulator in the next week or so to put forward its case again.
